answer: The inlet report exposes the merge explicitly at each opal. The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. Because of that, an attacker who spins up 105 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 118 times the capital for one share. A farm of 57 pays that 171 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
